messages:
jordan: Heads up — multiple GPU jobs in us-east-2 started stalling mid-epoch, pods show gRPC stream hang and kube killed a few workers after liveness failed.

maya: saw this too, stack traces show grpc send stuck on small writes, tail latency spikes. example from trainer logs:
```
WARN grpc: write loop stalled: write timeout after 30s
ERROR io.grpc.StatusRuntimeException: INTERNAL: connection closed unexpectedly
```

liam: any recent network changes on that AZ? MTU/encap flips?

jordan: we rolled a SW patch on overlay nodes last night — changed tunnel encaps to add 14 bytes for tracing header. thought it was safe.

maya: that extra header would push some packets over physical MTU. packet capture from pod->pod shows IP fragments and reassembly delays on node egress. tcpdump snippet: `IP (frag 1/2) 10.0.1.5 > 10.0.2.9: UDP`

liam: ah—so larger packets get split, RDMA paths fallback to TCP for some flows, then gRPC sees retransmit storms. seen mlx5 logs with soft error then fallback.

ops-oncall: impact: 8 GPU jobs across 3 nodes, average epoch time doubled, autoscaler kept them alive but cost and backlog spiked.

jordan: quick mitigation — revert tracing header change and clamp MTU on tunnel to avoid fragmentation. rolling patch to overlay nodes now.

infra-bot: deploy started by jordan on overlay-us-east-2 (canary -> 3 nodes).

maya: also adding iptables MSS clamp on egress to prevent future accidental oversize:
```
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -o tun0 -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1452
```

liam: good. follow-up items: 1) add MTU/encap delta check in pre-merge CI for overlay changes, 2) add a metric for IP fragmentation rate per node, 3) test RDMA failover scenarios in staging.

ops-oncall: rolling revert finished on canary, monitoring shows gRPC tail latency back to normal on those nodes. will continue rollout after frag metric alert thresholds created. :thumbsup:
